deliverables.text: A Brewster-angle worksheet: using the glass window's refractive index (Appendix A) and the Brewster-angle relationship, evaluate the inverse trigonometric function needed to find the window's own Brewster angle, showing algebra and the exact inverse trig function used.

A rotation-tolerance worksheet: starting from the rotation model in Appendix D, solve the resulting trigonometric equation, for each of the two shoot dates, for the rotation-offset angle at which total transmitted glare reaches the stated production tolerance, over the interval 0 to 90 degrees, showing every step of the algebra.

An identity-verification worksheet: using the Pythagorean identity, verify algebraically that sin^2(theta) = 1 - cos^2(theta) holds, then apply that verified identity to express each shoot date's transmitted-glare function in an alternate form and show both forms agree.

A percent-glare-removed comparison table: for the August Call and the September Call, compute the percent of the glass window's own specular glare a perfectly-tuned polarizer removes at each shoot's real incidence angle, and state the margin between the two options.

An original visual (Challenge 2b): a graph of transmitted-intensity fraction versus polarizer rotation-offset angle for both shoot dates overlaid, with the window's Brewster angle marked and each date's best-achievable-residual floor labeled.

balance.argument_a: The August 19, 2026, 2:00 PM shoot puts the real sun-incidence angle at about 55.9 degrees, within roughly 1 degree of the glass window's own 56.66-degree Brewster angle under the real, live-verified NOAA sun position for that date/time — reflected light there is very nearly fully polarized, so a well-tuned filter removes about 99.96 percent of the window's own glare, and the date is independently confirmed by real WDFW government count data (957 fish, the 2026 season's single highest day) to be the season's best Chinook day.
balance.argument_b: The September 22, 2026, 2:00 PM shoot captures a real, different, non-substitutable species (Coho) inside its own real, documented peak-viewing window (the last two weeks of September) — the closing salmon-viewing opportunity of the season — and while its real sun-incidence angle (about 44.4 degrees) sits measurably farther from the glass's 56.66-degree Brewster angle, a perfectly-tuned polarizer still removes about 90.3 percent of the window's own glare, a genuinely usable professional shot, not a ruined one; a producer valuing species completeness over the roughly 10 percent optical gap has real grounds to choose it.
balance.margin_basis: Compare (R - R_p/2)/R x 100 (percent of the glass window's own Fresnel reflectance removable by a perfectly-tuned polarizer) between the August Call's and the September Call's real sun-incidence angles, using the already-sourced refractive-index/Fresnel formulas (carried over from the-locks-window's S2/S3/S4) and freshly-sourced NOAA Solar Calculator readings for both 2026 dates.
balance.computation_note: case-research pass (2026-08-31): relative margin = (99.961-90.300)/90.300*100 = 10.70%, computed from live-re-verified NOAA readings (Aug 19 2026 14:00 PDT az 199.48/elev 53.55; Sep 22 2026 14:00 PDT az 199.23/elev 40.77) and Fresnel-derived percent-of-own-glare-removed (99.961% Aug vs 90.300% Sep) under n_glass=1.52 and the south-facing MA1 orientation. This confirms the design-phase preliminary estimate (~10.7%) almost exactly -- an independent re-derivation from freshly-fetched sources, not a copy. IMPORTANT CAVEAT surfaced this pass: the margin is NOT robust to the MA1 orientation assumption -- it inverts (Option B wins) under two of the four untested alternative orientations (135 deg SE, 270 deg W). It IS robust to the MA2 (call-time) and MA3 (September-date) assumptions across their tested ranges, and the winning option never changes across the 1-3 PM / Sept 15-29 sensitivity grid. See RESEARCH_LOG.md and FACILITATOR.md for full detail.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The underground viewing-room glass window's outward-facing compass orientation (surface normal azimuth)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public floor plan or engineering drawing states the window's exact compass bearing. Two independently fetched sources place the fish ladder / viewing room on the south side of the Locks complex (S11, plus independent corroboration).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Flips the dilemma. Re-checked across five candidate orientations (90/135/180/225/270 deg): at 180 (used) and 225, Option A wins (+10.7%, +6.6% relative margin); at 135 and 270, the margin inverts and Option B wins (-8.9%, -7.3%); at 90 it widens to +26.6%. Due-south is the only orientation with a documentary basis; the others are shown only to disclose the sensitivity honestly.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Exact shoot time on both stated dates
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public record states an actual scheduled call time for either shoot. A shared, mid-afternoon, same-convention time keeps the two dates on an apples-to-apples footing.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Checked 1:00 PM, 2:00 PM (used), 3:00 PM PDT under MA1. Option A stays ahead throughout (13.98% -> 10.70% -> 2.35% relative margin) -- margin narrows toward late afternoon but never crosses zero across this range.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The exact date within the real Coho peak-viewing window used for the September Call
modeling_assumptions.basis: The real Coho peak window is documented as a range (last two weeks of September, Sept 16-30) by converging sources (S6, S7), not a single official day the way August 19 is pinned down by live WDFW count data. September 22 is the numeric midpoint of that window.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Checked Sept 15, 22 (used), 29, all 2:00 PM PDT. Margin widens later in the window (6.97% -> 10.70% -> 15.16%) as the sun drops toward the equinox -- the midpoint date is a conservative pick, not one chosen to maximize the margin.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The stated production glare tolerance used in Challenge D2
modeling_assumptions.value_used: Tolerance = 2 x each date's own best-achievable residual (R_p/2)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No manufacturer or industry document states an acceptable on-set glare tolerance. Scaling the tolerance to each date's own physical floor (rather than a fixed absolute number) is a disclosed scenario choice.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Solving I(theta)=tolerance at 1.5x, 2x (used), 3x the residual: August's rotation-offset answer barely moves (~0.8 -> 1.1 -> 1.6 deg); September's moves substantially (~13.4 -> 19.1 -> 27.6 deg). The tolerance choice matters far more for September's worksheet answer.

sensitivity_note: NONE (SPEC §6). This is an engineering/optics and professional-scheduling trade-off; the endangered-species framing (Chinook salmon / Southern Resident orca population) is factual and sourced, not exploitative. Facilitators should keep tone documentary and factual, not alarmist, carried over unchanged from the superseded case's own sensitivity_note.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: The viewing-room window's exact compass bearing cannot be found in any public floor plan or engineering drawing (modeling_assumptions MA1). The due-south value used is a documented good-faith estimate from the closest available public analogue -- two independently fetched sources describing which side of the Locks complex the fish ladder/viewing room sits on (S11 and a corroborating search), not a direct measurement of the window's own bearing. This is the case's own disclosed, dilemma-flipping assumption: cases/the-late-run/sensitivity_model.py's mechanical MA1 sweep confirms the winner flips to Option B at two of four untested orientations (135 deg SE, 270 deg W), matching modeling_assumptions[MA1].sensitivity and FACILITATOR.md's 'The margin' and 'Twist' sections.
